content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks are the meat of the thigh portion of a chicken, commonly prepared as stewed dishes. When stewed, the skin stays soft and edible, adding extra flavor and richness. Drumsticks are a good source of protein, B‑vitamins, and essential minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks are featured in traditional dishes worldwide, from Russian stews to Asian braises.
Stewing retains more moisture than frying, keeping the meat juicy.
The skin left on the drumstick provides healthy fats and collagen, beneficial for skin and joints.
In some cultures, chicken drumsticks are considered a “power food” because of their high protein content.
Slow cooking allows aromatic spices to penetrate the meat, creating a deep, complex flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken drumsticks provide high‑quality protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain niacin (B3), vitamin B6, and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Drumsticks supply phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bone health and immunity.

items.title: Collagen in the skin
items.content: Edible skin contains collagen that may benefit skin, hair, and joint health.

items.title: Relatively low fat compared to other poultry parts
items.content: When excess fat is trimmed and the skin is eaten in moderation, drumsticks remain a relatively lean protein source.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Fat content in the skin
items.content: The skin contains saturated fats; people monitoring cholesterol should consume it sparingly.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken can harbor salmonella; ensure internal temperature reaches at least 74 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Sodium from seasoning
items.content: Stewed drumsticks are often seasoned with salt and sauces, which can increase sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot stewed drumsticks with sides such as potatoes, rice, or vegetables. The skin can be eaten together with the meat or removed for a leaner option. Pair with sauces like tomato, cream, or mustard for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked stewed drumsticks in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for 2‑3 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
